stories.headline: Election Day: Here is the No. 1 issue we're watching as a signal for stocks
stories.summary: Markets are closely monitoring election outcomes as a key signal for equity direction on November 3, 2026. Political uncertainty has historically driven volatility in stock performance.
stories.why_matters: Election results can shift policy expectations around fiscal spending, regulation, and tax rates that directly affect corporate earnings.

stories.headline: Oil edges up after report of US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
stories.summary: Oil prices show geopolitical sensitivity with reports of US military activity near Iran's strategic island. Crude is down $1.88 to $103.37 but remains volatile amid Middle East tensions.
stories.why_matters: Energy price swings influence inflation expectations and corporate profit margins across transportation and manufacturing sectors.

stories.headline: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng says hackers used fake job interviews, AI tool to steal $6.3 billion in crypto
stories.summary: Binance reported a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft exploiting fake job interviews and AI tools used by bad actors. The breach highlights growing cybersecurity risks in digital asset custody.
stories.why_matters: Large-scale crypto losses can trigger credit stress in affiliated financial institutions and increase regulatory scrutiny on digital asset safeguards.

calendar.note: Jobs data on Nov 6 will signal labor market health and influence Fed policy expectations as markets digest election results.
Post-election policy uncertainty gauge will reflect how much political outcomes shift market positioning on fiscal and regulatory fronts.

concept.title: Election-Day Volatility & Yield Curve Flattening
concept.one_liner: US equity gains on election day coincide with 10Y yield compression and rising VIX, signaling cautious positioning ahead of policy clarity.
concept.explanation: The S&P 500 gained 0.30% while the 10Y Treasury fell 3 bps and VIX rose 1.73 points, a mixed signal typical of election-day uncertainty. The 2Y/10Y curve continues to flatten with the 2Y up 3 bps while the 10Y declined, reflecting near-term Fed policy caution versus longer-term growth concerns. Elevated VIX and falling long yields suggest investors are hedging equity exposure until post-election policy direction becomes clearer.
concept.market_link: Investors should watch Friday's employment report for confirmation of labor market resilience; a soft jobs print could trigger yield curve inversion deeper and equities lower if growth fears dominate.

narrative: US equities ticked higher on election day (+0.30%) while bond markets priced in mixed signals: the 10Y fell 3 bps but the 2Y rose 3 bps, flattening the curve amid lingering policy uncertainty. VIX edged up 1.73 to 21.15, reflecting cautious hedging, while oil slipped $1.88 on demand concerns despite geopolitical tension.
